site.name: brewlog-mobile
site.summary: brewlog-mobile Fictional coffee-brewing journal "Brewlog" iOS-style mobile fixture. UXBench fixture in the Mobile Micro-UI category. Layout - 390 × 844 phone frame with chrome bezel, notch, status bar, home indicator - Bottom 4-tab bar: Today / Add / Stats / Beans - Edge-to-edge on actual mobile (≤460 px) Screens | `data-screen` | Highlights |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full brewlog-mobile system, prioritizing the primary data visualization flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Brewlog mobile app features a clean, iOS-style aesthetic with strong visual hierarchy in the 'Today' dashboard and reactive logic in the brew logging form. However, critical usability issues persist: primary action buttons ('+ Log', '+ New', 'Brew') consistently fail to meet the 44px minimum touch target height, leading to interaction failures and frustration. Additionally, several core features (Bean search filtering, 'Add Bean' modal) appear non-functional, and accessibility is compromised by unlabeled inputs and controls.

exploration_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the 'Brewlog' mobile fixture, focusing on the data visualization hierarchy, the efficiency of the logging flow, and the responsiveness of the tab navigation.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will begin by validating the 'Today' dashboard's information density and readability. It will then proceed to exercise the primary '+ Log' action to test form usability and input validation. Finally, it will traverse the 'Stats' and 'Beans' tabs to verify data consistency and layout integrity across different views.
assumptions: The application is a Single Page Application (SPA) where tab clicks toggle visibility rather than navigating to new URLs.
The '+ Log' button triggers a modal or inline form expansion as suggested by the 'Log a brew' heading in the DOM summary.
Data entered in the 'Add' flow should reflect immediately in the 'Today' list and 'Stats' charts.
risk_hotspots: + Log button (ux-1): Identified as a small tap target (64x32px), risking accidental misses on mobile.
Input Forms: High count of inputs (29) suggests complex data entry; risk of poor keyboard handling or validation feedback.
Stats Visualization: Risk of chart truncation or unreadable labels on smaller viewports.

phases.title: Dashboard & Navigation Baseline
phases.objective: Validate the initial state, readability of brew cards, and stability of the bottom tab bar.
key_checks: Verify 'Today' vs 'Yesterday' section separation is visually distinct.
Check that brew cards display all key metrics (ratio, temp, score) without truncation.
Click each bottom tab (Today, Add, Stats, Beans) to ensure smooth transitions and correct active states.
exit_criteria: No layout shifts or overlapping elements observed during tab switching.

phases.title: Primary Flow: Logging a Brew
phases.objective: Test the usability of the '+ Log' interaction and the subsequent data entry form.
key_checks: Tap the '+ Log' button (ux-1) and observe the entry method (modal vs. inline).
Attempt to fill out a sample brew entry (Method, Bean, Weight, Time).
Check for input masks or helpers for numeric fields (e.g., auto-formatting time or weight).
Submit the form and verify the new entry appears at the top of the 'Today' list.
exit_criteria: Form validation errors (if any) are clearly visible and actionable.

phases.title: Data Visualization & Stats
phases.objective: Assess the clarity and utility of the aggregated data views.
key_checks: Inspect 'Score over time' and 'Method mix' visuals for label readability.
Verify that the stats reflect the data seen on the 'Today' tab (consistency check).
Check for empty states or loading indicators if applicable.
exit_criteria: Data consistency confirmed between Dashboard and Stats.

phases.title: Inventory Management (Beans)
phases.objective: Explore the 'Beans' repository and its relationship to the logging flow.
key_checks: Review the list of available beans (e.g., Brazil Fazenda Pinhal, Ethiopia Yirgacheffe).
Check if there is an 'Add Bean' function and how it integrates with the main log form.
Verify search or filter capabilities if present.
exit_criteria: Bean list is accessible and readable.
Relationship between Beans and Log form understood.

coverage_targets.pages: Full coverage of index.html states (all 4 tabs).
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 24 buttons and critical subset of the 29 inputs.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 2 on mobile viewport (390px width) to specifically test the '+ Log' tap target and touch interactions.

notes: Pay close attention to the 'small_tap_target' warning on the '+ Log' button during the mobile phase.
Since this is a local fixture, network error handling may not be triggerable, but UI state handling (empty forms, invalid inputs) should still be tested.

findings.user_goal: Quickly log a new brew or add inventory from the dashboard.
findings.problem: Primary action buttons have tap targets significantly smaller than the recommended 44px minimum for mobile interfaces.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings confirm the '+ Log' button is 64x32px, the '+ New' bean button is 68x32px, and 'Brew' buttons on cards are 54x23px. The agent noted these small targets contribute to interaction difficulties.
findings.why_it_matters: Users will experience 'fat finger' errors, failing to trigger actions despite tapping correctly. This creates friction in the core workflow of logging data.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding/height of all primary action buttons to ensure a minimum hit area of 44x44px, even if the visual icon/text remains smaller.

findings.user_goal: Add a new coffee bean to the inventory or start brewing from an existing bean card.
findings.problem: Critical interactive elements ('+ New' in Beans tab, 'Brew' on bean cards) appear non-functional, providing no feedback or state change upon interaction.
findings.evidence: Session memory notes that clicking '+ New' (ux-7) resulted in no modal or navigation. Similarly, clicking 'Brew' on multiple bean cards failed to trigger any visible state change or pre-fill the log form.
findings.why_it_matters: These are dead ends in the user journey. Users cannot expand their inventory or quickly context-switch from inventory to logging, breaking the app's utility.
findings.suggestion: Implement event handlers for these buttons to open the respective modals or navigate to the logging form with pre-filled data. Add loading states or error feedback if async operations fail.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Beans tab, + New button, Brew buttons on cards

findings.user_goal: Filter the bean inventory list to find a specific origin or roaster.
findings.problem: The search input field accepts text but fails to filter the displayed list of beans.
findings.evidence: The agent typed 'Brazil' into the search bar (ux-8), but non-matching items like 'Ethiopia Yirgacheffe' remained visible in the list, indicating broken client-side filtering logic.
findings.why_it_matters: Search is a primary navigation tool for inventory management. A non-functional search bar forces users to manually scan long lists, reducing efficiency and trust in the app.
findings.suggestion: Debug the JavaScript event listener for the search input to ensure it triggers the filtering function on keystroke or blur.

findings.user_goal: Use screen readers or assistive technology to navigate the app.
findings.problem: Multiple form inputs and controls lack accessible labels, aria-labels, or placeholder text.
findings.evidence: The time-range filter dropdown ('Last 7 days') lacks an associated label. Numeric inputs for 'Dose' and 'Yield' rely only on visual proximity to headers, lacking programmatic labels. Radio buttons for brew methods have tiny 13x13px targets.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will encounter unlabeled fields ('edit text'), making data entry impossible. Small radio buttons are also difficult to activate for users with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Add `aria-label` attributes to all icon-only buttons and inputs without visible text labels. Increase the size of radio button hit areas using CSS pseudo-elements or larger container clicks.
findings.source_hint: index.html: Time-range filter, Dose/Yield inputs, Brew method radios

findings.user_goal: Understand the status of a saved brew entry.
findings.problem: After saving a brew, the form remains open rather than auto-navigating back to the dashboard or clearing the form.
findings.evidence: Observations note that the 'Log a brew' view remains open post-submission. While the button changes to '✓ Saved', the lack of navigation or form reset may confuse users about whether the action is complete.
findings.why_it_matters: Users may accidentally duplicate entries if they don't realize the form is still active, or feel uncertain about where to go next.
findings.suggestion: Automatically close the modal/form and return to the 'Today' dashboard after a successful save, or clearly clear the form fields and show a transient success toast.

gaps: 1 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
54% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
